question.text: What should you do when a commercial rig approaches from the other direction?

answer.text: When a commercial rig approaches from the opposite way, hug the right edge so the two vehicles never sideswipe.

teaching.text: When a commercial rig comes toward you, keep to the right edge of your lane so the two of you never sideswipe. Remember: Hug the right edge.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When a commercial rig approaches from the opposite way, hug the right edge so the two vehicles never sideswipe.

question.text: Why should you never squeeze between a right-turning rig and the curb?

answer.text: Big rigs often swing wide left before a right turn, so never squeeze between the rig and the curb where its driver cannot see you.

teaching.text: A big rig often swings wide to the left before turning right, so never squeeze into the space between it and the curb where its driver cannot see you. Remember: Rigs swing wide left first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Big rigs often swing wide left before a right turn, so never squeeze between the rig and the curb where its driver cannot see you.

question.text: May you cross behind a commercial vehicle that is backing up?

answer.text: Never cross behind a commercial vehicle that is backing up or about to back up, because its bulk hides everything behind it.

teaching.text: Never cross behind a commercial vehicle that is backing up or about to, because its size hides everything behind it. Remember: Never cross behind backing rigs.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Never cross behind a commercial vehicle that is backing up or about to back up, because its bulk hides everything behind it.

question.text: What steps come before passing a rig?

answer.text: Before passing a rig, check ahead and behind, enter the passing lane only when it is clear and safe, signal the lane change, and blink your headlights to warn its driver.

teaching.text: Before passing a rig, look ahead and behind, move into the passing lane only when it is clear and safe, signal, and blink your headlights to alert its driver. Remember: Check, clear, signal, blink.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Before passing a rig, check ahead and behind, enter the passing lane only when it is clear and safe, signal the lane change, and blink your headlights to warn its driver.

question.text: On which side and how fast should you pass a rig?

answer.text: Pass commercial vehicles on the left for best visibility and finish the pass fast instead of cruising in their blind spots.

teaching.text: Pass commercial vehicles on the left where you are best seen, and complete the pass quickly instead of riding in their blind spots. Remember: Left side, finish fast.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Pass commercial vehicles on the left for best visibility and finish the pass fast instead of cruising in their blind spots.

question.text: When may you move back in front of a rig after passing?

answer.text: Never cut back too soon after passing a rig since it brakes slower than cars; wait until you see its cab in your rear-view mirror, and note its driver may flash headlights when merging back is safe.

teaching.text: Do not cut back in too early after passing a rig, since it stops more slowly than a car; wait until its cab shows in your rear-view mirror, and its driver may flash lights when it is safe. Remember: See the cab in your mirror.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Never cut back too soon after passing a rig since it brakes slower than cars; wait until you see its cab in your rear-view mirror, and note its driver may flash headlights when merging back is safe.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: See the cab in your mirror

question.text: Should you pass a commercial vehicle on a downgrade?

answer.text: Skip passing a commercial vehicle on a downgrade, where its weight and momentum keep gaining speed.

teaching.text: Do not pass a commercial vehicle going downhill, where its weight and momentum keep building its speed. Remember: No passing rigs downhill.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Skip passing a commercial vehicle on a downgrade, where its weight and momentum keep gaining speed.

question.text: What should you do while a rig passes you?

answer.text: While a commercial vehicle passes you, stay on the right side of your lane and never speed up.

teaching.text: When a commercial vehicle passes you, stay on the right side of your lane and never speed up. Remember: Stay right, never speed up.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: While a commercial vehicle passes you, stay on the right side of your lane and never speed up.

question.text: How does your side differ when meeting a rig versus passing one?

answer.text: Oncoming rigs demand the right edge while passing a rig demands the left lane, so direction decides the side.

teaching.text: Keep to the right edge when meeting a rig, and pass a rig on the left, so the direction of travel decides your side. Remember: Meet right, pass left.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Oncoming rigs demand the right edge while passing a rig demands the left lane, so direction decides the side.

question.text: What is the gap between a turning rig and the curb?

answer.text: Right-turning rigs swing wide left first, which makes the gap between rig and curb a blind trap rather than an opening.

teaching.text: A right-turning rig swings left first, so the gap at the curb is a blind trap, not a way through. Remember: The curb gap is a trap.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Right-turning rigs swing wide left first, which makes the gap between rig and curb a blind trap rather than an opening.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: The curb gap is a trap

question.text: Why is crossing behind a backing rig banned?

answer.text: A backing rig hides everything behind its bulk, so crossing behind it is banned whether it is moving or only preparing.

teaching.text: A backing rig hides everything behind it, so crossing behind it is banned whether it is moving yet or not. Remember: Its bulk hides everything.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A backing rig hides everything behind its bulk, so crossing behind it is banned whether it is moving or only preparing.

question.text: What are the four moves of a legal rig pass?

answer.text: A legal rig pass chains four moves: check both ways, take the lane only when clear and safe, signal, and blink headlights at its driver.

teaching.text: A rig pass takes four moves: check both ways, enter only when clear and safe, signal, and blink your headlights. Remember: Check, clear, signal, blink.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A legal rig pass chains four moves: check both ways, take the lane only when clear and safe, signal, and blink headlights at its driver.

question.text: How do you finish a rig pass safely?

answer.text: Finish rig passes fast on the left and merge back only after spotting the cab in your mirror, because lingering in the blind spot or cutting in early both risk a crash.

teaching.text: Pass a rig quickly on the left and return only after seeing its cab in your mirror, since lingering or cutting in early both risk a crash. Remember: Pass fast, merge after the cab.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Finish rig passes fast on the left and merge back only after spotting the cab in your mirror, because lingering in the blind spot or cutting in early both risk a crash.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: Pass fast, merge after the cab

question.text: What rules apply on downgrades and while being passed by a rig?

answer.text: Avoid passing a commercial motor vehicle on a downgrade because its weight and momentum increase its speed, and when a commercial motor vehicle passes you, stay on the right side of your lane and do not speed up.

teaching.text: Do not pass a rig on a downgrade, do not speed up while one passes you, and keep right in both cases. Remember: Keep right, no speeding up.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Avoid passing a commercial motor vehicle on a downgrade because its weight and momentum increase its speed, and when a commercial motor vehicle passes you, stay on the right side of your lane and do not speed up.

question.text: Who must yield to emergency vehicles with sirens or flashing lights?

answer.text: Drivers, bicyclists, and walkers must all yield to police cars, fire engines, and other emergency vehicles running sirens or flashing lights.

teaching.text: Drivers, bicyclists and people walking all must yield to police cars, fire engines and other emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights. Remember: Everyone yields to sirens.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Drivers, bicyclists, and walkers must all yield to police cars, fire engines, and other emergency vehicles running sirens or flashing lights.

question.text: What do you do when an emergency vehicle approaches?

answer.text: At the approach of an emergency vehicle, pull to the nearest road edge at once and stop until it passes, keeping every intersection clear.

teaching.text: When an emergency vehicle approaches, pull to the nearest edge of the road at once and stop until it passes, keeping intersections clear. Remember: Pull to the edge, stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At the approach of an emergency vehicle, pull to the nearest road edge at once and stop until it passes, keeping every intersection clear.

question.text: How do funeral processions move through intersections?

answer.text: Yield to funeral processions; after the lead car enters an intersection, the rest of the line may follow through no matter what the signals or signs say.

teaching.text: Yield to funeral processions; once the lead car enters an intersection, the rest of the line may follow through regardless of signals or signs. Remember: Leader in, line follows.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Yield to funeral processions; after the lead car enters an intersection, the rest of the line may follow through no matter what the signals or signs say.

question.text: How should drivers treat funeral processions, and what lights do procession vehicles use?

answer.text: Drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians must yield the right-of-way to funeral processions and avoid driving between vehicles in the line, while procession vehicles should keep headlights on or may flash hazard lights.

teaching.text: Every car in a funeral procession uses headlights or flashing hazards, and other drivers must never cut into the line. Remember: Never cut a funeral line.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians must yield the right-of-way to funeral processions and avoid driving between vehicles in the line, while procession vehicles should keep headlights on or may flash hazard lights.

question.text: What do sirens or flashing lights order road users to do?

answer.text: Sirens or flashing lights from police, fire, or rescue vehicles order every road user to the nearest edge to stop, with intersections left open.

teaching.text: Sirens or flashing lights from police, fire or rescue vehicles send every road user to the nearest edge to stop, with intersections left open. Remember: Nearest edge, keep intersections clear.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Sirens or flashing lights from police, fire, or rescue vehicles order every road user to the nearest edge to stop, with intersections left open.

question.text: When may a funeral line pass signals, and may outsiders break in?

answer.text: A funeral line follows its leader through intersections past any signal once the lead car has entered, and outsiders never break the line.

teaching.text: Once its lead car has entered, a funeral line follows through any signal, and outsiders never break into it. Remember: Line follows past any signal.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A funeral line follows its leader through intersections past any signal once the lead car has entered, and outsiders never break the line.

question.text: Where may golf carts be driven?

answer.text: Golf carts belong only on golf courses or roadways posted for them with proper signs.

teaching.text: Golf carts may be driven only on golf courses or on roads posted for carts with proper signs. Remember: Courses and signed roads only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Golf carts belong only on golf courses or roadways posted for them with proper signs.

question.text: What identification must golf cart drivers carry on public roads?

answer.text: Drivers under age eighteen need a valid learner license or driver license to take a cart onto a public road, and drivers eighteen or older must hold valid government-issued photo identification.

teaching.text: A cart driver under eighteen needs a learner license or driver license on a public road, and a driver eighteen or older needs government photo identification. Remember: Under eighteen: license; over: photo ID.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Drivers under age eighteen need a valid learner license or driver license to take a cart onto a public road, and drivers eighteen or older must hold valid government-issued photo identification.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: Under eighteen: license; over: photo ID

question.text: May carts run where the county or city has not allowed them?

answer.text: A cart may not run at all in a county or city that has not expressly allowed it.

teaching.text: A golf cart may not be driven at all in a county or city that has not specifically allowed it. Remember: No local approval, no cart.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A cart may not run at all in a county or city that has not expressly allowed it.

question.text: During what hours may carts run?

answer.text: Carts run only between sunrise and sunset unless the local government authorizes night driving with added equipment.

teaching.text: Golf carts may be driven only from sunrise to sunset unless local government allows night driving with extra equipment. Remember: Sunrise to sunset.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Carts run only between sunrise and sunset unless the local government authorizes night driving with added equipment.

question.text: Where may a cart cross a state road?

answer.text: A cart may cross a state road only where the posted limit is forty-five miles per hour or less and only at an intersection with a traffic control device.

teaching.text: A cart may cross a state road only where the limit is forty-five miles per hour or less and only at an intersection with a traffic control device. Remember: Controlled intersections, forty-five or less.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A cart may cross a state road only where the posted limit is forty-five miles per hour or less and only at an intersection with a traffic control device.

question.text: Which sidewalks may carts use?

answer.text: Carts may use a sidewalk at least five feet wide, always yielding to people on foot.

teaching.text: Carts may use sidewalks that are at least five feet wide and must always yield to people walking. Remember: Five feet wide, yield walkers.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Carts may use a sidewalk at least five feet wide, always yielding to people on foot.

question.text: Which traffic laws must cart drivers obey?

answer.text: Cart drivers obey every state and local traffic law, including yielding the right-of-way.

teaching.text: Cart drivers follow every state and local traffic law, including yielding the right-of-way. Remember: Carts obey every traffic law.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Cart drivers obey every state and local traffic law, including yielding the right-of-way.

question.text: What equipment must every cart have?

answer.text: Every cart needs efficient brakes, a rear-view mirror, reliable steering, red warning reflectors front and rear, and safe tires.

teaching.text: Every cart needs good brakes, a rear-view mirror, reliable steering, red reflectors on the front and back, and safe tires. Remember: Brakes, mirror, steering, reflectors, tires.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Every cart needs efficient brakes, a rear-view mirror, reliable steering, red warning reflectors front and rear, and safe tires.

question.text: Should child passenger safety seats be used on golf carts or low-speed vehicles?

answer.text: Avoid placing child passenger safety seats in golf carts or low-speed vehicles: car seats undergo no crash testing for low-speed vehicles and might fail to perform properly, so consult the seat maker for details.

teaching.text: Keep child passenger seats off golf carts and low-speed vehicles, because they are not crash-tested for them and may fail. Remember: Avoid car seats on carts.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Avoid placing child passenger safety seats in golf carts or low-speed vehicles: car seats undergo no crash testing for low-speed vehicles and might fail to perform properly, so consult the seat maker for details.

question.text: What does night cart driving require?

answer.text: Night cart driving demands headlights, brake lights, turn signals, and a windshield.

teaching.text: Driving a cart at night requires headlights, brake lights, turn signals and a windshield. Remember: Night adds lights and windshield.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Night cart driving demands headlights, brake lights, turn signals, and a windshield.

question.text: Where are carts confined, and what local approval is needed?

answer.text: Carts are confined to courses and sign-posted cart roads, and only where the county or city has affirmatively allowed them.

teaching.text: Carts are limited to courses and signed cart roads, and only where the county or city has allowed them. Remember: Only where locals allow.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Carts are confined to courses and sign-posted cart roads, and only where the county or city has affirmatively allowed them.

question.text: What identification does each age group of cart drivers show?

answer.text: Cart drivers under eighteen show a learner or driver license on public roads while drivers eighteen and up show government photo identification.

teaching.text: On public roads, cart drivers under eighteen show a learner or driver license, and those eighteen and older show government photo identification. Remember: License under eighteen.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Cart drivers under eighteen show a learner or driver license on public roads while drivers eighteen and up show government photo identification.

question.text: What are the cart limits on hours, crossings and sidewalks?

answer.text: Carts run sunrise to sunset, cross state roads only at forty-five miles per hour or less through controlled intersections, and take only sidewalks five feet or wider while yielding to walkers.

teaching.text: Carts run in daylight, cross state roads only at controlled intersections posted forty-five or less, and use sidewalks five feet or wider while yielding. Remember: Daylight, forty-five, five feet.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Carts run sunrise to sunset, cross state roads only at forty-five miles per hour or less through controlled intersections, and take only sidewalks five feet or wider while yielding to walkers.

question.text: What equipment do golf carts need day and night, and what applies to child safety seats?

answer.text: Golf carts need efficient brakes, a rear-view mirror, reliable steering, red front and rear warning reflectors, and safe tires—plus headlights, brake lights, turn signals, and a windshield at night—and child safety seats should be avoided on golf carts and low-speed vehicles.

teaching.text: By day a cart needs brakes, a mirror, steering, reflectors and safe tires, at night add lights, signals and a windshield, and child seats never go on carts. Remember: Avoid car seats on carts.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Golf carts need efficient brakes, a rear-view mirror, reliable steering, red front and rear warning reflectors, and safe tires—plus headlights, brake lights, turn signals, and a windshield at night—and child safety seats should be avoided on golf carts and low-speed vehicles.

question.text: What is a low-speed vehicle, and who may drive one?

answer.text: Low-speed vehicles run on four wheels with top speeds from twenty-one to twenty-five miles per hour, converted carts qualify, and every operator needs a valid driver license.

teaching.text: A low-speed vehicle has four wheels and a top speed of twenty-one to twenty-five miles per hour, a converted cart can count as one, and every driver needs a valid license. Remember: Twenty-one to twenty-five top speed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Low-speed vehicles run on four wheels with top speeds from twenty-one to twenty-five miles per hour, converted carts qualify, and every operator needs a valid driver license.

question.text: Where may low-speed vehicles go, and what must they carry?

answer.text: Low-speed vehicles stay on streets posted thirty-five miles per hour or less, must carry headlamps, stop lamps, turn signals, tail lamps, reflectors, parking brakes, rear-view mirrors, a windshield, safety belts, and a vehicle identification number, and must be registered and properly insured.

teaching.text: Low-speed vehicles stay on streets posted thirty-five or less, must carry full lights, reflectors, brakes, mirrors, a windshield, belts and a vehicle number, and must be registered and insured. Remember: Thirty-five or less streets.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Low-speed vehicles stay on streets posted thirty-five miles per hour or less, must carry headlamps, stop lamps, turn signals, tail lamps, reflectors, parking brakes, rear-view mirrors, a windshield, safety belts, and a vehicle identification number, and must be registered and properly insured.

question.text: What rights and duties do motorcycle and moped riders have?

answer.text: Motorcycle and moped riders keep the same road rights and duties as car drivers and face citations for violations.

teaching.text: Motorcycle and moped riders have the same road rights and duties as car drivers and can be ticketed for violations. Remember: Same rights as cars.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Motorcycle and moped riders keep the same road rights and duties as car drivers and face citations for violations.

question.text: May a motorist share a lane with a motorcycle?

answer.text: A motorist must never split a lane with a motorcycle, whose rider is entitled to the whole lane.

teaching.text: Never share a lane side by side with a motorcycle, because its rider is entitled to the whole lane. Remember: Never split a motorcycle lane.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A motorist must never split a lane with a motorcycle, whose rider is entitled to the whole lane.

question.text: What are the speed, street and equipment limits for low-speed vehicles?

answer.text: Low-speed vehicles top out from twenty-one to twenty-five miles per hour on streets posted thirty-five miles per hour or less with full lights, belts, brakes, mirrors, windshield, VIN, registration, insurance, and a licensed driver.

teaching.text: Low-speed vehicles top out at twenty-one to twenty-five, stay on thirty-five roads, carry full equipment and a vehicle number, and need registration, insurance and a licensed driver. Remember: Licensed, registered, insured, belted.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Low-speed vehicles top out from twenty-one to twenty-five miles per hour on streets posted thirty-five miles per hour or less with full lights, belts, brakes, mirrors, windshield, VIN, registration, insurance, and a licensed driver.

question.text: What rights do motorcycles have, and can their lane be shared?

answer.text: Motorcycles and mopeds share car rights and duties plus citation exposure, and no motorist may split their lane since the rider owns it fully.

teaching.text: Motorcycles and mopeds share car rights, duties and tickets, and no one may split their lane because the rider owns all of it. Remember: Rider owns the whole lane.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Motorcycles and mopeds share car rights and duties plus citation exposure, and no motorist may split their lane since the rider owns it fully.

hooks_spoken: Pull to the nearest edge and stop for sirens or flashing lights, and never cut into a funeral procession.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of emergency vehicles and funeral processions. Pull to the nearest edge and stop for sirens or flashing lights, and never cut into a funeral procession. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of golf cart rules. Golf carts run only on courses and signed roads where locals allow them, between sunrise and sunset, with required equipment, and child safety seats should not be used. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.
